---
title: "Gallery"
description: "Every ddplot chart on one page. Filter by family or search by name."
---

Every chart in `ddplot`, grouped by what it is for and ordered by how often you are likely to need it. Click a card to see the chart's guide with live examples, or open its reference page for the full list of arguments.

```{r catalogue, include = FALSE}
categories <- list(
  list(id = "time-series", title = "Time series and trends",
       desc = "Lines, areas, streams and calendars for data that moves over time.",
       intro = "Charts for data indexed by time. `line_chart()` is the workhorse: it handles several series, `ts` objects, zooming, annotations and forecast ribbons. The others cover totals and their components, ranges, many categories at once, and daily patterns."),
  list(id = "comparisons", title = "Comparing categories",
       desc = "Bars, lollipops, dumbbells, slopes, ranks and bridges.",
       intro = "Charts for comparing values across categories, from the everyday bar chart to before/after comparisons, rankings over time and bridges that explain how a total was built. Most of them expect data that is already aggregated, one row per category; `dplyr::summarise()` is a convenient way to get there."),
  list(id = "distributions", title = "Distributions",
       desc = "Histograms, violins, swarms and ridgelines.",
       intro = "Charts that show how a numeric variable is spread: where values concentrate, how wide the spread is, and how several groups differ."),
  list(id = "relationships", title = "Relationships and flows",
       desc = "Scatter plots, hexbins and chord diagrams.",
       intro = "Charts for the relationship between two numeric variables, and for flows between categories."),
  list(id = "composition", title = "Part-to-whole and hierarchies",
       desc = "Pies, treemaps, waffles, sunbursts, mosaics and more.",
       intro = "Charts that split a whole into its parts, flat or nested."),
  list(id = "kpis", title = "KPIs and monitoring",
       desc = "Gauges, bullet charts, liquid fills and pulse grids.",
       intro = "Compact charts for dashboards: one value against its target or thresholds, or a grid that makes hot spots stand out."),
  list(id = "playful", title = "Playful indicators",
       desc = "Hearts, glasses, plants, flames and flowers.",
       intro = "Illustrative SVG indicators. They show a single level and are meant for presentations, landing pages and dashboards that need a lighter touch.")
)

catalogue <- read.csv(text = '
fn|category|name|use|tags
line_chart|time-series|Line chart|You track one or many series over time and want to zoom, compare and annotate|interactive,shiny
area_chart|time-series|Area chart|A single series where the volume under the line matters|
stacked_area_chart|time-series|Stacked area chart|You show a total and how each component contributes over time|interactive
area_band|time-series|Area band|You show a range over time, such as a min/max or an interval|
streamgraph|time-series|Streamgraph|Many categories change over time and the overall shape matters more than exact values|interactive
calendar_heatmap|time-series|Calendar heatmap|You look for daily, weekly or seasonal patterns in a daily series|interactive
anim_line_chart|time-series|Animated line chart|You present a single series and want it to draw itself on click|animated
bar_chart|comparisons|Bar chart|You compare a value across a handful of categories|
horz_bar_chart|comparisons|Horizontal bar chart|You have many categories or long labels|
lollipop_chart|comparisons|Lollipop chart|You want a lighter alternative to a bar chart|
horz_lollipop|comparisons|Horizontal lollipop|A lollipop chart with many categories or long labels|
dumbbell_chart|comparisons|Dumbbell chart|You show the gap between two values for each category|interactive
slope_chart|comparisons|Slope chart|You compare two points in time and want to show who rose and who fell|interactive
bump_chart|comparisons|Bump chart|You follow how rankings change over several periods|interactive
waterfall_chart|comparisons|Waterfall chart|You explain how a starting value becomes a final value|interactive
radar_chart|comparisons|Radar chart|You compare a few items across several variables|interactive
radial_bar_chart|comparisons|Radial bar chart|You show progress of a few items towards a goal|interactive
bar_chart_race|comparisons|Bar chart race|You animate a ranking through time for a presentation|animated
histogram|distributions|Histogram|You look at the distribution of a single numeric variable|
violin_plot|distributions|Violin plot|You compare distributions across groups, with quartiles|interactive
beeswarm_plot|distributions|Beeswarm plot|You want to show every observation, not only a summary|interactive
ridgeline_plot|distributions|Ridgeline plot|You compare the distributions of many groups|interactive
animated_histogram|distributions|Animated histogram|You present a distribution and want the bars to grow on click|animated
scatter_plot|relationships|Scatter plot|You look at the relationship between two numeric variables|
hexbin_plot|relationships|Hexbin plot|A scatter plot has too many points to read|interactive
chord_diagram|relationships|Chord diagram|You show flows between categories, such as migration or trade|interactive
pie_chart|composition|Pie and donut chart|You split a whole into a few parts|
treemap_chart|composition|Treemap|You split a whole into many parts, optionally nested|interactive
waffle_chart|composition|Waffle chart|You show shares as a grid of 100 squares|interactive
sunburst_chart|composition|Sunburst chart|You explore a hierarchy with several levels|interactive
mosaic_chart|composition|Mosaic chart|You show how two categorical variables combine|interactive
rose_chart|composition|Rose chart|You show a cyclical breakdown, such as months, Nightingale-style|interactive
parliament_chart|composition|Parliament chart|You show seats won by each party|
gauge_chart|kpis|Gauge|You show one value against warning and danger thresholds|
bullet_chart|kpis|Bullet chart|You show one value against a target and qualitative ranges|
liquid_chart|kpis|Liquid fill|You show a single percentage in an eye-catching way|animated
pulse_grid|kpis|Pulse grid|You want the hottest cells of a matrix to stand out|animated
heart_fill|playful|Heart fill|You show a level from 0 to 1 as a filling heart|
glass_fill|playful|Glass fill|You show a level from 0 to 1 as a filling glass|
plant_growth|playful|Plant growth|You show progress as a growing plant|
flame|playful|Flame|You show an intensity, such as an error count, as a flame|animated
flower|playful|Flower|You want a decorative, optionally rotating, flower|animated
', sep = "|", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
```

```{r gallery, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
esc <- function(x) htmltools::htmlEscape(x, attribute = TRUE)
short <- c("time-series" = "Time series", comparisons = "Comparisons",
           distributions = "Distributions", relationships = "Relationships",
           composition = "Part-to-whole", kpis = "KPIs", playful = "Playful")

chips <- c(
  sprintf('<button type="button" class="dd-chip active" data-filter="all">All <span>%d</span></button>', nrow(catalogue)),
  vapply(categories, function(cc) sprintf(
    '<button type="button" class="dd-chip" data-filter="%s">%s <span>%d</span></button>',
    cc$id, short[[cc$id]], sum(catalogue$category == cc$id)), "")
)

badge <- function(tags) {
  if (is.na(tags) || !nzchar(tags)) return("")
  t <- strsplit(tags, ",")[[1]]
  paste(sprintf('<span class="dd-badge dd-badge-%s">%s</span>', t, t), collapse = "")
}

cards <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(catalogue)), function(i) {
  r <- catalogue[i, ]
  sprintf(paste0(
    '<div class="dd-card" data-category="%s" data-search="%s">',
    '<div class="dd-thumb"><img src="../gallery/%s.png" alt="%s" loading="lazy"></div>',
    '<div class="dd-card-body">',
    '<div class="dd-card-meta"><span class="dd-card-cat">%s</span>%s</div>',
    '<h3 data-toc-skip><a class="stretched-link" href="%s.html#%s">%s</a></h3>',
    '<p>%s.</p>',
    '<a class="dd-card-ref" href="../reference/%s.html" title="Reference"><code>%s()</code></a>',
    '</div></div>'),
    r$category, esc(tolower(paste(r$fn, r$name, r$use, r$category, r$tags))),
    r$fn, esc(r$name), short[[r$category]], badge(r$tags),
    r$category, r$fn, esc(r$name), esc(r$use), r$fn, r$fn)
}, "")

cat('<div class="dd-gallery-tools">',
    '<input type="search" class="form-control dd-search" placeholder="Search charts, e.g. ranking, flows, KPI" aria-label="Search charts">',
    '<div class="dd-chips" role="group" aria-label="Filter by family">', chips, '</div>',
    '</div>',
    '<div class="dd-gallery">', cards, '</div>',
    '<p class="dd-empty" hidden>No chart matches your search.</p>', sep = "\n")
```
